edit.description: the teardown reaches the module's own liveness guard instead of re-deriving half of it; the already-exited case asserts the escalation it is titled for

summary: The suite's teardown re-derives `signalProcessTree`'s guard without `signalCode`, so every signal-killed case SIGKILLs a group whose leader is already reaped

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

acceptance: the suite's teardown signals through the module's own guard, so no case aims a signal at a pid the host has been free to re-hand; and the already-exited case asserts no escalation was armed instead of sleeping past the grace
pins: terminating a child that has already exited arms no escalation over its pid
notes: Verified this tick. `tests/processTree.test.ts:64` guards on `pid === undefined || exitCode !== null` alone; a signal-killed child has `exitCode === null` with `signalCode` set (measured), so three of six cases reach `process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL")` on a reaped group — the hazard `src/processTree.ts:131` guards and `:246` is titled for. That case asserts only `not.toThrow`, then sleeps 500ms with no verdict (`engineering.md`, *A green verdict is proven non-vacuous*).
